Problematic, see inline comments. The llite half changes behaviour for every client, not only for migrated files: a layout that arrives without a layout lock is now dropped instead of applied, and that breaks setting a layout through setxattr and then reading it back. A regression test for the migrate -EIO case belongs with this change too (or a pointer to the sanityn patch later in the series).

Uploaded patch set 2.

commit.subject: LU-21023 mdt: revoke the layout lock of a migrated file
commit.message:
LU-21023 mdt: revoke the layout lock of a migrated file

A migrated file gets a new FID on the target MDT but keeps its OST
objects. A client that still had the layout of the old FID cached
found the stripes already owned when it opened the new FID, and the
I/O failed with -EIO.

- mdt: in mdt_reint_migrate(), add MDS_INODELOCK_LAYOUT to the source
  lock of a regular file, so clients drop the layout cached under the
  old FID. Skip it for a released file, which has no OST objects and
  whose layout lock an HSM restore holds until it ends. Check
  migrate_hsm_allowed with the same HSM flags, before the lock.
- lov: in lov_conf_set(), keep a layout set without a layout lock
  (from an MDT reply) invalid, so the object of the new FID can take
  its stripes over (lov_init_sub() returns -EAGAIN for them).

Fixes: 1d6b96a1cf04 ("LU-15529 mdt: optimize dir migration locking")
